title: Abstaining from drink and drugs
summary: Brown says he never drinks or smokes, tells of taking a quart of milk to a San Francisco marijuana party, and says he learned from watching others.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And so your attitudes came from seeing -- observing the excesses of people around you, rather than any strict upbringing that you had? I thought perhaps this was something you were taught was bad, growing up in a religious home.

Well, I'm not too religious. I was in the most strict religious home. But I usually think for myself, and judge for myself. But, of course, I never -- a lot of things go on now that we never heard of. And -- but this attitude that I had that sort of guided me, with the experience that I'd seen. For instance, I've seen, oh, liquor flow like water. In fact, I have bought liquor for friends. But I never drink it. And as far as this -- I remember when marijuana and stuff became popular.
I remember distinctly one marijuana party. I never stayed away because they did it. I've been around plenty of it. But I remember they had one big marijuana party in
San Francisco, and I took a quart of milk.
So I said, 'I don't need that. I don't need nothing to make me feel any different.' After I'd seen them under the influence, I knew I didn't want to feel any different.
So that's just one of the peculiar things that have happened in my musical career.
